title: Suggestions for review
intro: Nothing here has been implemented. Each suggestion says what it would improve in decision making, what it would cost and what could go wrong, so it can be accepted, rejected or deferred before any code is written. The decision column is deliberately empty: choosing a path is the owner's call, not the build's.
how_to_use: Read the table, fill in the decision column, then implement only what was chosen. A suggestion is not a task until it is chosen.

rows.title: A single decision sheet for the next slate
rows.improves: Turns eight pages of research into one page that answers 'what is the call on each game'.
rows.proposal: Add a page that lists, for every game of the next slate, the three originated markets, the fair line, the market line, the difference and the model probability, with one row per game and a single action column.
rows.evidence: The own-lines page already produces every one of those fields; only the roll-up is missing.

rows.title: Publish every market every time it changes
rows.improves: Makes closing-line value measurable for the first time, which is the only way to tell whether the model adds information.
rows.proposal: Write a snapshot to the price store on every publication of every market, and refuse to publish a market that has no opening snapshot.
rows.evidence: 146 of the 172 originated snapshots have an opening number only. The store already refuses a close without an open; the rule just has to be obeyed by the publishers.

rows.title: Add a shadow board: record the pick before the market moves
rows.improves: Separates the model from the market's final answer, which is the only clean measurement of the model's own contribution.
rows.proposal: At every rebuild, snapshot the model line for the coming week and freeze it. Later, compare that frozen number with the closing line to get true closing-line value rather than a back-computed approximation.
rows.evidence: The walk-forward table already produces exactly this frozen number for past weeks, and the settlement file settles it against the results.

rows.title: License a price feed, or stop quoting market numbers
rows.improves: Makes a return on a spread or a total possible; today only the moneyline can carry money.
rows.proposal: Either obtain a licensed feed that records spread and total prices with timestamps, or remove the market columns from every table and publish the model lines alone.
rows.evidence: The pinned archive has spread and total lines without prices, and moneyline prices without opening prices.

rows.title: Fill the depth column from the official game books
rows.improves: Turns 'player is out' into 'a third-string player is starting', which is the difference between a fact and an estimate.
rows.proposal: Parse the participation table of the official game book PDF for the previous game of each club and publish the snap share of the replacement, with the tier derived from the published participation.
rows.evidence: Each official game page links its own game book PDF. The depth chart route is a 404, so the game book is the official route that remains open.

rows.title: Publish the injury band as columns, not as a footnote
rows.improves: Lets a reader see how much of a line depends on an injury judgement that has not been validated.
rows.proposal: For every game, publish the low, central and high injury band as three extra columns next to the fair line, and mark the band as an assumption wherever it appears.
rows.evidence: The band already exists in a sibling namespace's output and is not exposed in any table.

rows.title: A model-versus-closing-line panel with an automatic demotion
rows.improves: Stops a model that has drifted from the market from staying live.
rows.proposal: Add a rolling eight-week panel of the model's out-of-sample spread error against the closing line's, and demote a live strategy when the model trails over the window.
rows.evidence: The model currently trails the closing line by 0.43 points of average error over 89 games, and the demotion gate already has a rule for it.

rows.title: One results feed and one price store for the whole repository
rows.improves: Removes sixteen copies of the same official tables and the risk that two of them disagree.
rows.proposal: Make this namespace's results feed and price store the single source, and have the other NFL namespaces read them instead of keeping their own copies.
rows.evidence: Sixteen NFL namespaces each carry their own standings, slate and results snapshot, captured on different dates.

rows.title: Label every third-party number in the interface, not only in a footnote
rows.improves: Stops a reader from taking a market price for an official league number.
rows.proposal: Give every market column a visible third-party badge and keep the official source link beside it, rather than explaining the distinction once per page.
rows.evidence: The distinction is currently carried in a note under each table.

rows.title: Put a 'what this page can and cannot answer' header on every page
rows.improves: Stops a page being read as a recommendation when it is a measurement.
rows.proposal: Add a two-line header to each page: the question it answers and the question it does not.
rows.evidence: Every page in this namespace already carries a purpose note in the generator; the same wording is simply not surfaced as a header.

rows.title: A 'what changed since yesterday' panel
rows.improves: Turns a weekly site into a working monitor: the reader sees the new injuries and the moved lines, not the whole table again.
rows.proposal: Diff the official injury designations and the price snapshots against the previous run and publish only the differences, with a link to the full table.
rows.evidence: The injury report and the price store are both timestamped, so a diff is mechanical.

rows.title: Open the prop and parlay families, or state them closed
rows.improves: Says plainly whether two thirds of the competition is possible.
rows.proposal: Either license a player-prop price history and a joint-distribution source, or keep both families closed on the leaderboard with the missing input named.
rows.evidence: No prop or parlay price exists in any source in scope, and nfl.com publishes no betting lines at all.

rows.title: Unit tests for settlement and for the demotion transition
rows.improves: Protects the two pieces of logic that decide whether money is made.
rows.proposal: Add deterministic tests over synthetic fixtures: a push, a tie, a missing price, a strategy crossing the demotion threshold and a strategy crossing back.
rows.evidence: The demotion rule is currently only exercised by its own evaluation over real strategies, none of which is live.

rows.title: Publish the sample-size floor next to every rate
rows.improves: Stops a 30-bet hit rate from being read like a 300-bet one.
rows.proposal: Show n beside every rate and put a visible marker on any rate computed on fewer decisions than the gate floor.
rows.evidence: Every strategy row already carries n; only the leaderboard needs the marker.
